checks.finding: REQ-002–011 and AC-002–011 distinguish supported owners, preparation versus execution, immutable authorization inputs, reconciliation, verification and evidence. Deployment-specific targets and health expectations are explicit mandatory run inputs, not implicit implementation choices.

Recognizing existing ownership does not authorize unsupported execution: REQ-002, the non-goals and AC-002 consistently require blocking. Development approval is explicitly separate from cloud authorization. References to other features' historical artifacts establish baseline behavior, not premature implementation of this feature.

AC-002–012 cover conflicting ownership, import denial, input mutation, invalid approvals, concurrency, replay, uncertain submission, brownfield protection, unsupported profiles, unhealthy or missing observations, evidence tampering and unavailable credentials. Provider-specific tests cover Azure preview changes and AWS Change Set substitution.

Requirements fix GitHub Actions, Bicep and CDK as initial boundaries. Target scopes, federation, health probes, backup policy and budget are explicitly required before live deployment; missing values block live operation. Investigation records pinned upstream baselines and identifies adoption-time compatibility validation.

REQ-004–006, Roles and Permissions, AC-004–006 and Entry Point Safety require distinct authenticated prepare/apply approval at the write call site, immutable binding, replay protection and reconciliation without automatic resubmission. Cleanup requires separate authorization; production writes are excluded.

The twelve requirements have corresponding observable acceptance criteria, explicit supported paths, non-goals, trust boundaries and failure outcomes. Remaining architecture and contract details can be designed without inventing product authorization or success semantics.
The host states that the target project has no domain/ directory; investigation independently records domain-sync skipped for that reason.
